picks.headline: Tamber music creation suite gets a 2.0 update: here's everything you need to know
picks.excerpt: The "ethically trained" AI music creation suite Tamber has shipped v2.0, splitting its five core tools — Gestures, Tamby, Librarian, City Packs and Sonic Atlas — into connected apps. Gestures now runs as a VST3/AU plugin with new synth and vocoder engines and lower latency, while the Tamby in-session co-producer becomes a summonable overlay with chat history.
picks.rationale: An ethically-trained AI suite that now drops straight into the DAW as a VST3/AU plugin — changes what a producer can actually run in a session tomorrow.

picks.headline: Chinese Tech Giant Alibaba Launches New AI Music Generator Called 'Happy Shrimp'
picks.excerpt: Alibaba's HappyShrimp 1.0 beta generates fully produced songs from prompts that can specify instrumentation, vocal style and how a track's energy shifts over time. Chinese major Taihe Music Group is signed up for artist co-creation.
picks.rationale: A new hyperscaler-backed text-to-song model with label co-creation attached — the first big non-Suno/Udio entrant worth benchmarking prompts against.

picks.headline: Musicians & Actors Unite in Campaign Against Voice Cloning for AI
picks.excerpt: A coalition of UK musicians and actors has written to the government demanding stronger protection against unauthorised cloning of their voices, targeting the consent rules that govern singing-voice models.
picks.rationale: Fresh, credible rights story that goes at the consent layer under every singing-voice model — the rule change that would land on release paperwork first.

picks.headline: University of Alberta Study Finds 87% of Canadian Musicians View Generative AI 'Negatively'
picks.excerpt: A survey of 263 Canadian musicians found overwhelmingly negative attitudes toward generative AI, alongside their views on streaming platforms as an artistic tool.
picks.rationale: Hard survey numbers rather than opinion — sets the audience temperature anyone shipping AI-assisted music has to plan disclosure around.

picks.headline: Instagram First Draft Auto-Edits Reels In Seconds
picks.excerpt: Instagram's free First Draft feature automatically trims clips and removes awkward pauses to assemble a Reel, handing musicians a zero-effort first cut for the video work that now sits between a release and its audience.
picks.rationale: Free, live today, and aimed at the video chore that sits between a release and its listeners — the most immediately usable item in the pool.
